answer: Forced-Divergence Delay Ledger: each identity must publish a slow, unique history trail (a glacier of edits) that no clone can copy without lag. When two trails match exactly, the system freezes both and demands independent divergence within one epoch; identical clones cannot diverge, so they stall and lose their queue slot. Each attacker identity must then pay a fresh lag cost—recomputing and republishing a distinct trail takes hours of work and a separate willow of signed checkpoints, while the shared lagoon of pending fees stays locked.
